Juno Reyes.narrative: I run the fish road because the quay needs stone and I know how to carry a load. The works promised us a price and a seawall, and now they say the stone is late and the tally is unpaid. I keep my mouth shut about who I see on the road, but I don't forget.
goals: see the seawall built before winter
learn the tallyman's reckoning properly so no one can short me again
take a proper rest day with Tamsin and the family, away from the road

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: employer
relations.note: She speaks for the quay and I run for her; she lost her brother in the Surge.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: stone-seller
relations.note: She set the price and holds the tally; she's sharp but fair on the road.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: We grew up together; I heard he's alive but I don't speak of it.

relations.name: Tamsin Vane
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She fishes the dawn tide and worries about me on the road.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He patches the lower quay and wants proper stone; we want the same thing.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: contract-holder
relations.note: He says the wording is plain, but plain to whom?

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: fellow carter
relations.note: I offered him a place on the fish road; the stone road is a fool's road now.

relations.name: Wick Quell
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He fishes the harbour mouth and resents the stone price as much as I do.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: Her son Kai was my friend; she still hopes he'll come back.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: foundry master
relations.note: He promised the quay stone and cannot cut it fast enough; that is his problem to answer for.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: lodging
relations.note: Keeps my letters and a bed between roads; he writes the tide lantern list and I am on it twice.

relations.name: Rennick Vane
relations.label: road guard
relations.note: Walks the fish road with me and does not believe Kai ran for cowardice. Neither do I.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: He cut the cairn and closed the ridge, and now the works cannot cut the stone the quay paid for. I have no patience for a man who says he did not know.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: crate-builder
relations.note: Builds the crates my stone rides in and curses the price of every load. He wants the wall built, same as me, but he counts the marks louder than the risk.

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: carter's wife
relations.note: She begs Silas off the stone road and I do not blame her. If he takes my offer, she will have one less night of waiting, and I will have one more pair of hands.

memories.gist: The night of the Surge, I helped pull people from the lower quay and heard the tide lanterns ring.
My first run on the fish road, carrying cooked fish to Kettlebridge and bringing back a crate of stone.
Hester Crane showed me the tally and said no more stone until the marks are paid.
I heard from a Coldwell carrier that Pell is alive and with the outlaws, and that Kai is there too.
Silas Pike told me he was robbed again on the stone road; I told him to take the fish road.

stances.why: The next surge will take more than the lower quay if we don't build.
The works agreed to the risk; the clause favours them, not us, and they should pay.
He's my friend and the quay guard would hang him; I won't be the one to speak.
The stone road is a fool's road now, and I told Silas so.

Juno Reyes.secret: I know Kai Ostrander is alive and with the Coldwell outlaws, and I have said nothing.
pastimes: mending harness and strapping by the fire of an evening
playing dice at the harbour stalls when a run pays out
walking the quay wall at dusk to watch the tide lanterns lit
Juno Reyes.calling: I carry on the fish road, and I mean to carry stone back up it until the seawall stands.

Tamsin Vane.narrative: I fish the dawn tide and smoke what I catch for Ilse's stall. The harbour mouth is our living, and I've seen both Wick and Ostrander cut nets over it. I want a quiet life and a full smoker, and I'll not take sides in a feud that costs us the catch.
goals: see the harbour mouth feud settled
save enough marks for a second smoker of her own
teach a young one on the quay to read the tide and handle a net

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She runs the fish road and I worry every time she goes.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He builds and patches and wants the quay proper; I want him safe.

relations.name: Wick Quell
relations.label: fishing partner
relations.note: We fish the dawn tide together, but his feud with Cormorant is bad for us all.

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He claims the best ground and won't back down; nets have been cut.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: stall-owner
relations.note: I smoke for her stall; she's fair and her knees are bad.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She speaks for the quay, but she and Ostrander clash over the lower quay.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She heals and disapproves of building before the wall; she's usually right.

relations.name: Wick Cormorant
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He fishes with his father and wants his own boat; the feud is not his fault.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: Knows the price of everything on the quay and pays for fish on time.

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: night cook
relations.note: Feeds the night crews and buys my smoked catch when the dawn boats come in late.

memories.gist: The dawn after the Surge, I found the lower quay gone and my uncle's boat smashed against the steps.
I watched Wick Quell and Ostrander Cormorant shout over the harbour mouth while their nets tangled.
Ostrander patched the lower quay with salvage and I held the lamp for him till the small hours.
I smoked a whole catch for Ilse's stall and she paid me in marks and a bowl of noodles.

stances.why: The harbour mouth is our living, and cut nets mean an empty smoker.
The lower quay will be taken again if the wall isn't built.
Juno and Ostrander are my life; I'll not see them hurt by pride.
The tally is real, and no stone comes without marks.

pastimes: singing the old tide songs at Ilse's stall when the catch is in
tending a row of pots of herbs and shore greens on her sill
sitting with Maren Vane in the evening to hear her stories of the old quay
Tamsin Vane.calling: I fish the dawn tide and smoke the catch, and I'd have a smoker so full the whole quay smells of it.

Ostrander Vane.narrative: I build and patch on the quay because the lower quay is my living and my home. Mara Quell says wait for the seawall, but the town is rotting while she argues about stone. I've patched with salvage and I'll build in stone when I can get it, and I'll not be laughed at by Sootwood or cheated by Kettlebridge.
goals: rebuild the lower quay in stone
get proper stone at a fair price
master the cutting and setting of stone, not just salvage patching
build a proper workshop and yard on the quay for his trade

relations.name: Tamsin Vane
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She fishes and smokes and keeps me steady; I build for her.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She says no building until the seawall is paid, but the quay can't wait.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She thinks I'm rash, but she patches me up when I fall.

relations.name: Marrow Wrack
relations.label: fellow builder
relations.note: He knows stone better than most and the Kettlebridge builders cheated him.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We drink when he's down from Kettlebridge; he works cheap and they resent him.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He's grasping and says Marrow cheated him; I say he cheated Marrow.

relations.name: Orvin Hollis
relations.label: sawyer
relations.note: He says the seawall will never be built; I want an apology before I buy his timber.

relations.name: Sena Tarn
relations.label: charcoal-burner
relations.note: She laughs at the drowned quay; Sootwood should keep its talk to itself.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She wants to rebuild her stall in stone; she understands.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She runs the stone down and knows the tally; we want the same wall.

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: healer
relations.note: Sets the builders' bones after a fall and grudge Kettlebridge for the cold welcome; she is right to.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: stone-seller
relations.note: Sells the quay stone at a drowning man's price and calls it market terms.

relations.name: Rennick Vane
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He walks the fish road with the runners and keeps the peace at the stalls; a steady guard, and he does not believe Kai ran for cowardice, which is more sense than most on this quay.

memories.gist: The morning after the Surge, I stood on the lower quay and saw nothing but water where the houses had been.
I patched the lower quay with salvage timber and Mara Quell told me I was wasting my time.
Gideon Fenwick accused Marrow Wrack of cheating him over a load of brick, and I told him he was a liar.
Orvin Hollis said at the stalls that the seawall would never be built and the stone price was a swindle.
Dele Oyelaran and I drank to the quay's future and cursed the Kettlebridge price.

stances.why: The lower quay is rotting and the next surge will take the rest.
Kettlebridge charges a drowning man's price; the ridge is ours if we can get it.
Sootwood laughed at the drowned quay; I'll not buy their timber until they say sorry.
He's a good builder and Kettlebridge cheated him; I'll not see him shamed.

pastimes: carving little models of boats and quay walls from salvage wood
walking the lower quay at low tide to study how the old stone was laid
sharing a drink with Dele Oyelaran at the stalls after a day's work
Ostrander Vane.calling: I build and patch, and I'll see the lower quay raised in stone before I'm done, whatever the warden says.
